Jeremy Cunningham :: Passing Fires Posted on October 1, 2026 October 1, 2026 Jeremy Cunningham makes music that seems to be perpetually slipping out of its own frame. On Passing Fires , the Chicago drummer moves from free-jazz and skronk to electronics, funk, post-rock and pop, assembling a cast of improvisers, producers and singers who keep the music in motion. There are moments of muscular rhythmic interplay, strange electronic textures, children’s voices, whispered vocals and unexpected turns. It’s an album of restless curiosity, but never restlessness for its own sake: Cunningham’s drumming provides a steady gravitational pull as the music wanders. West Coast twilight, boot cuts, alternate takes, live excursions, stray transmissions and wayward frequencies. 34.1090° N, 118.2334° W Dur-Dur Band :: Volume 3 (1988) & Volume 4 (1989) Posted on September 30, 2026 September 29, 2026 The latest archival installment from the Somalian hotel band shows an unwieldy group streamlining their sound in the studio, dialing up the hooks, battening down the rhythms and keeping the grooves on point. Taking inspiration from Motown and disco as much as reggae and Afrobeat, the Dur-Dur Band kept the wild 70s alive even as the ugly 80s were taking over. Transmissions :: Johnny Marr Posted on September 30, 2026 October 1, 2026 Certain people play guitar in a way that is immediately recognizable, no matter the context. Our guest this week on Transmissions, Johnny Marr, is one such guitarists. A founding member of legendary indie band The Smiths, his sound is undeniable a blend of jangle, chime, bite, and attitude. He’s back with a new album The Age Of Everything, which he joins us to discuss. Along the way, we also get into the global influence of The Smiths, discuss how Black American musicians inspired his sound, and share some of his less apparent influences, including Neil Young, who if you hear Marr tell it, played a rather pivotal role in the development of British punk rock. Future Sounds Of Jazz Vol. 16 Posted on September 29, 2026 September 28, 2026 Future Sounds of Jazz Vol. 16 is both a forecast and a wormhole. The Aquarium Drunkard Guide to Across the Horizon Posted on September 25, 2026 September 27, 2026 What, exactly, is Across the Horizon? Asher White :: Love Aggregates Posted on September 24, 2026 September 23, 2026 Asher White goes maximalist on Love Aggregates , building heavy doses of orchestral power pop from her bedroom. Those Were the Days of Miracle and Wonder :: Paul Simon’s Graceland at 40 Posted on September 24, 2026 September 24, 2026 Paul Simon’s 1986 album Graceland exists in this weird state, an album that eternally evokes 1986, but always sounds so different from other albums of its era. It’s an collection that’s self absorbed, but also so relatable when the listener finds themselves hitting middle age. It brought world music to the forefront, but also presented a misleading picture. It’s a fascinating study in contrast and now, some 40 years later it’s an album we still can’t make up our minds about even as we listen to it for the hundredth time.
